title: Business quality and competitive position
summary: How the company makes money, what protects it from rivals, and what could go wrong, including how managers use the company's money. Figures are clues; the reasons need explaining.
unreliableWhen: When past margins are treated as a promise, when a strong brand or product is assumed to last for ever, or when a good business is treated as a reason to pay any price.
goodExample: A fictional food maker's margins hold steady while it pays dividends from free cash flow, a clue that something protects the business for now.
badExample: A fictional app maker with thin margins and rising debt: a 5% price cut forced by a rival would wipe out almost all its profit before tax.
